subject: maths
title: Primary 4 Fraction of a Set
seo_title: P4 Fraction of a Set Worksheets: Free Primary 4 Maths with Answers (MOE Syllabus)
standard_text: Fraction as part of a set
meta_desc: Free P4 fraction of a set practice: shaded fractions in simplest form, 3/5 of 35, finding the whole and bar model word problems. 100 questions with answers.
key_big: Divide by the denominator to find 1 unit, then multiply by the numerator.
body_html:
The big idea

A fraction of a set compares a part of the set with the whole set. The denominator tells you how many equal parts (units) the set is cut into. The numerator tells you how many of those parts you take.

What fraction is shaded?

Count the shaded objects and all the objects. Write shaded over all. Then simplify.

Finding a fraction of a set

To find 14 of a set, share it into 4 equal groups and take one group. This is the same as dividing by 4.

For a non-unit fraction such as 35, find 1 unit first (divide by the denominator), then multiply by the numerator.

Example

There are 40 pupils in a class. 34 of them walk to school. How many pupils walk?

4 units = 40. 1 unit = 40 ÷ 4 = 10. 3 units = 3 × 10 = 30.

Answer: 30 pupils

Finding the whole from a part

If you know a part, find 1 unit first. Then multiply by the number of units in the whole.

Example

25 of the beads in a box are red. There are 14 red beads. How many beads are in the box?

2 units = 14. 1 unit = 14 ÷ 2 = 7. The whole is 5 units: 5 × 7 = 35.

Answer: 35 beads

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do instead
Counting groups when the groups are not the same size (1 group out of 3 = 13)Count the objects: 2 shaded out of 12 = 16
Dividing by the numerator: 34 of 36 = 36 ÷ 3 × 4 = 48Divide by the denominator: 36 ÷ 4 = 9, then 3 × 9 = 27
Not simplifying: leaving the answer as 68Divide the numerator and the denominator by the same number: 68 = 34
Writing shaded over white (4 shaded, 2 white = 42)The denominator is all the objects: 4 out of 6 = 23

faq.q: What is fraction of a set in P4 maths?
faq.a: It means finding a part of a group of objects, such as 3/4 of 20 counters. Students also say what fraction of a set is shaded and find the whole set when they know a part.

faq.q: How do I explain 3/5 of 35 to my child?
faq.a: Draw a bar of 5 equal units for 35, so 1 unit = 35 ÷ 5 = 7. Then 3 units = 3 × 7 = 21.

faq.q: What is the most common mistake in fraction of a set?
faq.a: Dividing by the numerator instead of the denominator. Another is counting groups of different sizes instead of counting the objects, and forgetting to give the answer in simplest form.

faq.q: Is fraction of a set in the MOE Primary 4 syllabus?
faq.a: Yes. The MOE 2021 Primary Mathematics Syllabus includes fraction as part of a set in Primary 4, with word problems solved using the model method.

items.q: What fraction of the counters is shaded? Give your answer in simplest form.
items.e: 2 out of 8 counters are shaded: 28. Divide the numerator and the denominator by 2: 28 = 14.

items.q: What fraction of the counters is shaded? Give your answer in simplest form.
items.e: 3 out of 9 counters are shaded: 39. Divide the numerator and the denominator by 3: 39 = 13.

items.q: What fraction of the squares is shaded? Give your answer in simplest form.
items.e: 4 out of 10 squares are shaded: 410. Divide the numerator and the denominator by 2: 410 = 25.

items.q: What fraction of the counters is shaded? Give your answer in simplest form.
items.e: 6 out of 8 counters are shaded: 68. Divide the numerator and the denominator by 2: 68 = 34. (The denominator is all the counters, not just the white ones.)

items.q: What fraction of the squares is shaded? Give your answer in simplest form.
items.e: 8 out of 12 squares are shaded: 812. Divide the numerator and the denominator by 4: 812 = 23. (The denominator is all the squares, not just the white ones.)

items.q: What fraction of the counters is shaded? Give your answer in simplest form.
items.e: 10 out of 12 counters are shaded: 1012. Divide the numerator and the denominator by 2: 1012 = 56. (The denominator is all the counters, not just the white ones.)

items.q: What fraction of the counters is not shaded? Give your answer in simplest form.
items.e: 12 − 3 = 9 counters are not shaded. 9 out of 12 counters are not shaded: 912. Divide the numerator and the denominator by 3: 912 = 34.

items.q: What fraction of the counters is not shaded? Give your answer in simplest form.
items.e: 20 − 8 = 12 counters are not shaded. 12 out of 20 counters are not shaded: 1220. Divide the numerator and the denominator by 4: 1220 = 35.

items.q: The counters are in equal groups. What fraction of the counters is shaded? Give your answer in simplest form.
items.e: There are 4 equal groups and 1 of them is shaded: 14 of the groups. Check with counters: 3 out of 12 counters = 312 = 14. (3 is the number of counters in one group, not the number of groups.)

items.q: The counters are in equal groups. What fraction of the counters is shaded? Give your answer in simplest form.
items.e: There are 5 equal groups and 2 of them are shaded: 25 of the groups. Check with counters: 6 out of 15 counters = 615 = 25. (3 is the number of counters in one group, not the number of groups.)

items.q: The counters are in equal groups. What fraction of the counters is shaded? Give your answer in simplest form.
items.e: There are 6 equal groups and 4 of them are shaded: 46 of the groups. Check with counters: 12 out of 18 counters = 1218 = 23. (3 is the number of counters in one group, not the number of groups.)

items.q: The counters are in equal groups. What fraction of the counters is shaded? Give your answer in simplest form.
items.e: There are 4 equal groups and 3 of them are shaded: 34 of the groups. Check with counters: 15 out of 20 counters = 1520 = 34. (5 is the number of counters in one group, not the number of groups.)

items.q: The counters are in 3 groups. What fraction of all the counters is shaded? Give your answer in simplest form.
items.e: The groups are not the same size, so do not count groups (1 group out of 3 gives the wrong answer). Count counters: 2 out of 12 are shaded. 212 = 16.

items.q: The counters are in 3 groups. What fraction of all the counters is shaded? Give your answer in simplest form.
items.e: The groups are not the same size, so do not count groups (1 group out of 3 gives the wrong answer). Count counters: 5 out of 10 are shaded. 510 = 12.

items.q: The counters are in 3 groups. What fraction of all the counters is shaded? Give your answer in simplest form.
items.e: The groups are not the same size, so do not count groups (2 groups out of 3 gives the wrong answer). Count counters: 8 out of 16 are shaded. 816 = 12.

items.q: What fraction of the squares is green? Give your answer in simplest form.
items.e: 4 out of 12 squares are green: 412. Divide both by 4: 13. (Do not count the orange squares, and the denominator is all 12 squares.)

items.q: What fraction of the squares is coloured (green or orange)? Give your answer in simplest form.
items.e: Coloured: 6 + 4 = 10 out of 15 squares: 1015. Divide both by 5: 23.

items.q: Which set has 23 of its counters shaded?
items.e: 23 = 46, so 4 out of 6 counters must be shaded. That is picture C. A has 2 shaded out of 5, so it shows 25. B has 2 shaded out of 6, so it shows 13. D has 3 shaded out of 6, so it shows 12.

items.q: Which set has 34 of its counters shaded?
items.e: 34 = 912, so 9 out of 12 counters must be shaded. That is picture B. A has 3 shaded and 4 white, so it shows 37. C has 8 shaded out of 12, so it shows 23. D has 6 shaded out of 10, so it shows 35.

items.q: Wei Ming says 69 of the counters are shaded. What is 69 in simplest form?
items.e: Divide the numerator and the denominator by 3: 6 ÷ 3 = 2 and 9 ÷ 3 = 3, so 69 = 23. (Do not divide only the numerator, and do not subtract 3 from each number.)

sets.title: Find a unit fraction of a set

items.q: The counters are in equal groups. What is 14 of 12?
items.e: The 12 counters are in 4 equal groups. One group is 14 of the set. One group has 3 counters. (4 is the number of groups, not the answer.)

items.q: The counters are in equal groups. What is 13 of 15?
items.e: The 15 counters are in 3 equal groups. One group is 13 of the set. One group has 5 counters. (3 is the number of groups, not the answer.)

items.q: The counters are in equal groups. What is 15 of 20?
items.e: The 20 counters are in 5 equal groups. One group is 15 of the set. One group has 4 counters. (5 is the number of groups, not the answer.)

items.q: The counters are in equal groups. What is 16 of 18?
items.e: The 18 counters are in 6 equal groups. One group is 16 of the set. One group has 3 counters. (6 is the number of groups, not the answer.)

items.q: The counters are in equal groups. What is 12 of 14?
items.e: The 14 counters are in 2 equal groups. One group is 12 of the set. One group has 7 counters. (2 is the number of groups, not the answer.)

items.q: Find 14 of 20.
items.e: 14 of 20 means 20 shared into 4 equal groups. 20 ÷ 4 = 5.

items.q: Find 13 of 27.
items.e: 13 of 27 means 27 shared into 3 equal groups. 27 ÷ 3 = 9.

items.q: Find 18 of 40.
items.e: 18 of 40 means 40 shared into 8 equal groups. 40 ÷ 8 = 5.

items.q: Find 17 of 56.
items.e: 17 of 56 means 56 shared into 7 equal groups. 56 ÷ 7 = 8.

items.q: Find 19 of 63.
items.e: 19 of 63 means 63 shared into 9 equal groups. 63 ÷ 9 = 7.

items.q: Find 16 of 48.
items.e: 16 of 48 means 48 shared into 6 equal groups. 48 ÷ 6 = 8.

items.q: Find 15 of 85.
items.e: 15 of 85 means 85 shared into 5 equal groups. 85 ÷ 5 = 17.

items.q: Find 14 of 96.
items.e: 14 of 96 means 96 shared into 4 equal groups. 96 ÷ 4 = 24.

items.q: Find 13 of 120.
items.e: 13 of 120 means 120 shared into 3 equal groups. 120 ÷ 3 = 40.

items.q: There are 32 children at the void deck. 14 of them are playing badminton. How many children are playing badminton?
items.e: 14 of 32 means 32 shared into 4 equal groups. 32 ÷ 4 = 8 children.

items.q: Mdm Wong has 30 mandarin oranges. She gives 15 of them to her neighbour. How many oranges does she give away?
items.e: 15 of 30 means 30 shared into 5 equal groups. 30 ÷ 5 = 6 oranges.

items.q: A box has 24 crayons. 16 of them are red. How many crayons are not red?
items.e: Red: 24 ÷ 6 = 4 crayons. Not red: 24 − 4 = 20 crayons. (4 is the number of red crayons, and 18 comes from 24 − 6.)

items.q: Siti has 45 stickers. She gives 19 of them to Nurul. How many stickers does Siti have left?
items.e: She gives 45 ÷ 9 = 5 stickers. Left: 45 − 5 = 40 stickers. (Take away 5, not 9.)

items.q: Ali takes 13 of 24 sweets. Ryan takes 14 of 24 sweets. How many more sweets does Ali take than Ryan?
items.e: Ali: 24 ÷ 3 = 8. Ryan: 24 ÷ 4 = 6. 8 − 6 = 2 more sweets. (4 − 3 = 1 compares the denominators, not the sweets.)

items.q: 15 of 40 is the same as 12 of what number?
items.e: 15 of 40 = 40 ÷ 5 = 8. 8 is half of 16, because 16 ÷ 2 = 8. (8 is 15 of 40; 4 is half of 8.)

items.q: The counters are in equal groups. What is 23 of 12?
items.e: Make 3 equal groups of 4. 23 of 12 is 2 groups: 2 × 4 = 8.

items.q: The counters are in equal groups. What is 34 of 16?
items.e: Make 4 equal groups of 4. 34 of 16 is 3 groups: 3 × 4 = 12.

items.q: The counters are in equal groups. What is 25 of 15?
items.e: Make 5 equal groups of 3. 25 of 15 is 2 groups: 2 × 3 = 6.

items.q: The counters are in equal groups. What is 35 of 20?
items.e: Make 5 equal groups of 4. 35 of 20 is 3 groups: 3 × 4 = 12.

items.q: The counters are in equal groups. What is 56 of 18?
items.e: Make 6 equal groups of 3. 56 of 18 is 5 groups: 5 × 3 = 15.

items.q: The model shows 35 split into 5 equal units. Find 35 of 35.
Find 23 of 27.
Find 34 of 32.
Find 47 of 49.
Find 58 of 64.
Find 310 of 90.
items.e: 10 units = 90. 1 unit = 90 ÷ 10 = 9. 3 units = 3 × 9 = 27. (Divide by the denominator 10, not the numerator 3.)

items.q: Find 79 of 54.
Find 25 of 100.
items.e: 5 units = 100. 1 unit = 100 ÷ 5 = 20. 2 units = 2 × 20 = 40. (Divide by the denominator 5, not the numerator 2.)

items.q: Find 49 of 72.
items.e: 9 units = 72. 1 unit = 72 ÷ 9 = 8. 4 units = 4 × 8 = 32. (Divide by the denominator 9, not the numerator 4.)

items.q: Find 68 of 24.
items.e: 68 = 34. 1 unit = 24 ÷ 4 = 6. 3 units = 3 × 6 = 18. (Or 1 unit = 24 ÷ 8 = 3, and 6 units = 18.)

items.q: There are 40 pupils in a class. 38 of them wear spectacles. How many pupils wear spectacles?
items.e: 8 units = 40. 1 unit = 40 ÷ 8 = 5. 3 units = 3 × 5 = 15 pupils.

items.q: There are 28 marbles in a bag. 27 of them are red. How many marbles are not red?
items.e: 1 unit = 28 ÷ 7 = 4. Red: 2 units = 8 marbles. Not red: 5 units = 5 × 4 = 20 marbles. (8 is the number of red marbles.)

items.q: Mr Tan has 36 rambutans. He gives away 56 of them. How many rambutans does he give away?
items.e: 6 units = 36. 1 unit = 36 ÷ 6 = 6. 5 units = 5 × 6 = 30 rambutans.

items.q: How much more is 23 of 30 than 34 of 24?
items.e: 23 of 30: 30 ÷ 3 × 2 = 20. 34 of 24: 24 ÷ 4 × 3 = 18. 20 − 18 = 2.

items.q: 34 of 20 is the same as 13 of what number?
items.e: 34 of 20 = 20 ÷ 4 × 3 = 15. 15 is 13 of 15 × 3 = 45. (15 is 34 of 20, not the number we want.)

sets.title: Find the whole from a part

items.q: 13 of a number is 8. What is the number?
items.e: 13 of the number is 8, so 1 unit = 8. The whole is 3 units: 3 × 8 = 24. (Multiply to find the whole; do not divide.)

items.q: 14 of a number is 12. What is the number?
items.e: 14 of the number is 12, so 1 unit = 12. The whole is 4 units: 4 × 12 = 48. (Multiply to find the whole; do not divide.)

items.q: 25 of a number is 14. What is the number?
items.e: 2 units = 14. 1 unit = 14 ÷ 2 = 7. The whole is 5 units: 5 × 7 = 35.

items.q: 34 of a number is 27. What is the number?
items.e: 3 units = 27. 1 unit = 27 ÷ 3 = 9. The whole is 4 units: 4 × 9 = 36.

items.q: 15 of a number is 9. What is the number?
items.e: 15 of the number is 9, so 1 unit = 9. The whole is 5 units: 5 × 9 = 45. (Multiply to find the whole; do not divide.)

items.q: 16 of a number is 7. What is the number?
items.e: 16 of the number is 7, so 1 unit = 7. The whole is 6 units: 6 × 7 = 42. (Multiply to find the whole; do not divide.)

items.q: 23 of a number is 18. What is the number?
items.e: 2 units = 18. 1 unit = 18 ÷ 2 = 9. The whole is 3 units: 3 × 9 = 27.

items.q: 56 of a number is 40. What is the number?
items.e: 5 units = 40. 1 unit = 40 ÷ 5 = 8. The whole is 6 units: 6 × 8 = 48.

items.q: 38 of a number is 15. What is the number?
items.e: 3 units = 15. 1 unit = 15 ÷ 3 = 5. The whole is 8 units: 8 × 5 = 40.

items.q: 49 of a number is 32. What is the number?
items.e: 4 units = 32. 1 unit = 32 ÷ 4 = 8. The whole is 9 units: 9 × 8 = 72.

items.q: 37 of a number is 24. What is the number?
items.e: 3 units = 24. 1 unit = 24 ÷ 3 = 8. The whole is 7 units: 7 × 8 = 56.

items.q: 58 of a number is 35. What is the number?
items.e: 5 units = 35. 1 unit = 35 ÷ 5 = 7. The whole is 8 units: 8 × 7 = 56.

items.q: These 6 counters are 14 of a set. How many counters are in the whole set?
items.e: 14 of the number is 6, so 1 unit = 6. The whole is 4 units: 4 × 6 = 24 counters. (Multiply to find the whole; do not divide.)

items.q: These 10 counters are 23 of a set. How many counters are in the whole set?
items.e: 2 units = 10. 1 unit = 10 ÷ 2 = 5. The whole is 3 units: 3 × 5 = 15 counters.

items.q: 12 of the children at a playground are girls. There are 13 girls. How many children are at the playground?
items.e: 12 of the number is 13, so 1 unit = 13. The whole is 2 units: 2 × 13 = 26 children. (Multiply to find the whole; do not divide.)

items.q: 34 of the counters in a box are blue. There are 18 blue counters. How many counters are there in the box?
items.e: 3 units = 18. 1 unit = 18 ÷ 3 = 6. The whole is 4 units: 4 × 6 = 24 counters.

items.q: 27 of the beads in a jar are red. There are 10 red beads. How many beads are not red?
items.e: 2 units = 10, so 1 unit = 5. Not red: 7 − 2 = 5 units = 5 × 5 = 25 beads. (35 is all the beads.)

items.q: 35 of the pupils in a group are boys. There are 12 boys. How many girls are there?
items.e: 3 units = 12, so 1 unit = 4. Girls: 5 − 3 = 2 units = 2 × 4 = 8 girls. (20 is the whole group.)

items.q: Hafiz gave away 15 of his cards. He had 16 cards left. How many cards did he have at first?
items.e: He gave away 1 unit, so 16 cards are the other 4 units. 4 units = 16, 1 unit = 4. At first: 5 units = 20 cards. (16 is not 15 of the cards.)

items.q: Priya used 35 of her beads to make a bracelet. She had 14 beads left. How many beads did she have at first?
items.e: She used 3 units, so 5 − 3 = 2 units are left. 2 units = 14, 1 unit = 7. At first: 5 units = 35 beads. (14 is 2 units, not 3 units.)

items.q: There are 40 pupils in a class. 34 of them walk to school. How many pupils walk to school?
items.e: 4 units = 40. 1 unit = 40 ÷ 4 = 10. 3 units = 3 × 10 = 30 pupils. (10 pupils do not walk.)

items.q: There are 36 pupils in a class. 59 of them take the school bus. How many pupils do not take the school bus?
items.e: 1 unit = 36 ÷ 9 = 4. The bus takes 5 units, so 9 − 5 = 4 units do not. 4 × 4 = 16 pupils. (20 pupils take the bus.)

items.q: A hawker stall sold 60 plates of chicken rice in the morning. 25 of them were roasted chicken rice. How many plates of roasted chicken rice were sold?
items.e: 1 unit = 60 ÷ 5 = 12. 2 units = 2 × 12 = 24 plates. (Divide by 5, the denominator, not by 2.)

items.q: Mrs Lim baked 48 curry puffs for a school fair. She sold 58 of them. How many curry puffs were left?
items.e: 1 unit = 48 ÷ 8 = 6. She sold 5 units, so 3 units were left: 3 × 6 = 18 curry puffs. (30 curry puffs were sold.)

items.q: Mr Tan bought 72 mandarin oranges for Chinese New Year. He gave 56 of them to his relatives. How many oranges did he give away?
items.e: 1 unit = 72 ÷ 6 = 12. 5 units = 5 × 12 = 60 oranges.

items.q: Devi and her mother made 30 oil lamps for Deepavali. They painted 35 of the lamps. How many lamps were not painted?
items.e: 1 unit = 30 ÷ 5 = 6. Not painted: 5 − 3 = 2 units = 2 × 6 = 12 lamps. (18 lamps were painted.)

items.q: There are 180 pupils at Sports Day. 29 of them run in a relay race. How many pupils run in the relay race?
items.e: 1 unit = 180 ÷ 9 = 20. 2 units = 2 × 20 = 40 pupils. (90 comes from 180 ÷ 2.)

items.q: There are 120 Primary 4 pupils. 38 of them are in a sports CCA. The rest are in other CCAs. How many pupils are in other CCAs?
items.e: 1 unit = 120 ÷ 8 = 15. Sports: 3 units = 45. Other CCAs: 5 units = 5 × 15 = 75 pupils.

items.q: 14 of the books on a shelf are storybooks. There are 9 storybooks. How many books are on the shelf?
items.e: 1 unit = 9. The shelf has 4 units: 4 × 9 = 36 books. (27 is the number of books that are not storybooks.)

items.q: Hui Min gave away 25 of her stickers. She had 18 stickers left. How many stickers did she have at first?
items.e: She gave away 2 units, so 3 units are left. 3 units = 18, 1 unit = 6. At first: 5 units = 30 stickers. (45 comes from taking 18 as 2 units.)

items.q: 35 of the pupils on a school bus are girls. There are 15 girls. How many boys are on the bus?
items.e: 3 units = 15, so 1 unit = 5. Boys: 2 units = 2 × 5 = 10 boys. (25 is all the pupils on the bus.)

items.q: Sarah collected 54 shells at East Coast Park. 49 of them were white. How many shells were not white?
items.e: 1 unit = 54 ÷ 9 = 6. White: 4 units = 24. Not white: 9 − 4 = 5 units = 5 × 6 = 30 shells. (24 shells were white.)

items.q: Ali has 24 coins. 13 of them are 50¢ coins and the rest are 20¢ coins. How much money are the 50¢ coins worth?
items.e: 50¢ coins: 24 ÷ 3 = 8 coins. 8 × 50¢ = 400¢ = $4. ($3.20 is the value of the 16 coins of 20¢.)

items.q: Jun Jie has 32 marbles. 38 of them are blue and the rest are green. How many more green marbles than blue marbles does he have?
items.e: 1 unit = 32 ÷ 8 = 4. Green has 5 units and blue has 3 units, so green has 2 more units: 2 × 4 = 8 more marbles. (12 blue and 20 green.)

items.q: At a void deck party, 37 of the people are adults and the rest are children. There are 12 more children than adults. How many people are at the party?
items.e: Adults: 3 units. Children: 7 − 3 = 4 units. The difference is 1 unit = 12. Altogether: 7 units = 7 × 12 = 84 people.

items.q: 23 of the tables at a hawker centre are taken. 14 tables are empty. How many tables are taken?
items.e: Taken: 2 units. Empty: 1 unit = 14. Taken: 2 × 14 = 28 tables. (42 is all the tables.)

items.q: Priya has 45 stickers. She gives 15 of them to Kavya and 13 of them to Arjun. How many stickers does she have left?
items.e: Kavya: 45 ÷ 5 = 9. Arjun: 45 ÷ 3 = 15. Given away: 9 + 15 = 24. Left: 45 − 24 = 21 stickers.

items.q: There were 48 people in an MRT train. At a station, 14 of them got off and 9 people got on. How many people were in the train then?
items.e: Got off: 48 ÷ 4 = 12. 48 − 12 = 36. Then 9 got on: 36 + 9 = 45 people. (27 comes from taking away the 9 people instead of adding them.)

items.q: A basket has 56 rambutans. 47 of them are ripe. Kumar eats 5 of the ripe rambutans. How many ripe rambutans are left?
items.e: 1 unit = 56 ÷ 7 = 8. Ripe: 4 units = 32. After Kumar eats 5: 32 − 5 = 27 rambutans.

items.q: In a choir, the number of boys is 23 of the number of girls. There are 27 girls. How many pupils are in the choir?
items.e: Girls: 3 units = 27, so 1 unit = 9. Boys: 2 units = 18. Altogether: 5 units = 5 × 9 = 45 pupils. (18 is the number of boys only.)
